newsitem.title: FRANCE: Counterfeit seizures up sharply at Paris airports.
newsitem.headline: Counterfeit seizures up sharply at Paris airports.

text.p: French customs said seizures of counterfeit goods at the Paris airports in the first nine months of 1996 rose sharply on the same period the previous year.

January-September 1996 counterfeit goods seized at Orly airport between January-September 1996 totalled 163,800 items, up 228 percent on the same period in 1995 while at Charles de Gaulle counterfeit goods seized totalled 81,461 items, an increase of 38 percent, French customs figures show.
"The vast majority of these items were designated commercial freight and were found during inspections of aircraft containers," a customs official told Reuters.
Orly and CDG airports accounted for 58.7 percent of the global number of counterfeit goods seized at French frontier posts which totalled 417,800 items, up 53.6 percent on January-September 1995.

French customs had devoted more resources to uncovering international traficking networks for counterfeit goods since the introduction of tougher legislation in February 1994 for this type of offence and this resulted in an increase in theems seized in recent years, the official added.
The top six orginating countries for counterfeit goods destined for France or transiting French territory in the first nine months of 1996 Thailand, China and Hong Kong, Italy, Taiwan and the U.S.

Clothing and clothing accessories acounted for 34 percent of counterfeit goods seized followed by automotive parts, watches and jewelry, sunglasses, audio and video cassettes, C.Ds, computer progammes and perfumes.
Last month, at Orly airport, French customs seized around 60,000 counterfeit watches in a shipment from Hong Kong and destined for the Mexican market.

In the same shipment, customs officers discovered counterfeit goods made up of 6,000 items of underwear and 950 tee-shirts - destined for the African market and a batch of 2,160 tee-shirts and shorts, manufactured in Bangkok, which were to have been on-forwarded to Madagacar.

"This seizure is indicative of the upsurge in the international trafficking of counterfeit goods and confirms the importance of this phenomenon in some Far East countries," he added. --Reuters Air Cargo NewsRoom Tel +44 171 542 5017 Fax *5017
